subject: Biotechnology
title: Cold Chain and Drug Stability
description: A 60-second lesson on Cold Chain and Drug Stability.

hook.text: Biologics are proteins — leave them warm and they unfold, aggregate, or degrade. The cold chain keeps them alive.

buildup.text: Most antibodies require 2 to 8°C storage — mRNA vaccines initially needed minus 70°C with dry ice shipping.

discovery.text: Lyophilization freeze-dries proteins into powder — stable at room temperature for months, reconstituted before use.

twist.text: Cold chain failures destroy $35 billion in drugs annually — temperature excursions are a global health problem.

climax.text: Thermostable formulations with trehalose sugars protect proteins without refrigeration — crucial for remote clinics.

punchline.text: Keep it cold or lose the cure — stability is the last mile of biologics.

quiz.question: How does lyophilization improve biologic drug stability?
options: It converts proteins into small molecules that resist heat
Freeze-drying removes water, creating a stable powder that can be stored without refrigeration
It permanently changes the protein structure to tolerate higher temperatures
